title: the map offset of the lane ground truth (0.3 - 1 m per element and drive, worst in Boston) lowers the metric by city and shows up as a per-scene lateral bias of correct predictions

a.recipe: analysis script temp/loop20/e252_gt_offset.py on the cached raw outputs of champion, e24_j1eq_s0, e24_j1rc_s0 (VAL 873): the frames of boston-seaport
a.note: per-city pooling inside the script; the arms of this card name the two groups of frames, not two checkpoints

c.recipe: the same models, the frames of the three Singapore locations

rule.note: city gap Boston - Singapore, read from the printout (the tool cannot split by city): CAP when Q(Boston) is lower by >= 0.03 for all three models with non-overlapping 95 % scene intervals AND the share of correct points with |lateral offset| > 0.5 m is >= 1.5 x that of Singapore; NO EVIDENCE when the Q gap is < 0.01

kill: none (CPU, 1 thread, about 10 min); void if the frame count per city does not add up to 873 or the identity check (offset of the GT against itself) is not exactly 0
